findings.reason: the worker must either enumerate merge commits in a second pass or the conflict resolution is silently unreviewed, and since that resolution is runtime source, dropping it makes `changes_runtime_source` read False and lets `carry_review_forward` re-stamp a review over a runtime change no reviewer read.
findings.text: the deliverable specifies `rev-list --no-merges tip ^integration_ref ^older` and then says it "adds any path a merge commit in that set shows in its combined diff, so a conflict resolution the run wrote is kept", but `--no-merges` removes exactly those commits: on `fc7f245289` (the §1 run's own merge) `git rev-list --merges fc7f245289 ^main` names 1 commit while the `--no-merges` form names none of them, and on the plan's second named instance `14c9d487fb` — the conflict-resolved merge over `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py` — `rev-list --no-merges 14c9d487fb ^main` is empty and `git show --cc --name-only 14c9d487fb` names that one path, so the path the section promises to keep is the path the specified command drops

findings.reason: the done-when asserts `changes_runtime_source` is False, which is correct either way, and the repair it asks for is unaffected; only the sentence claiming what happens next overstates, so a worker reading it may expect a carry that the code declines and report a surprise rather than a wrong change.
findings.text: §3 states that with the corrected paths "a run whose own delta holds no runtime source … so `carry_review_forward` carries the stored review to the merge head and composes none", omitting the `touches_delivered_work` term that also gates the carry (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1206`, `:1220`), so a delta that is a test and an evidence fragment — the very case the done-when asserts — is declined rather than carried when those paths are the ones the reviewed diff delivered

findings.reason: the one mechanism the section adds beyond filtering is the merge-combined-diff union, and without a conflicted merge in the fixture the gate cannot fail on its absence, so the node can go green while carrying a runtime-source conflict resolution unreviewed.
findings.text: the fixture holds "a merge of an integration branch that carries many unrelated files" and a further run commit, so the merge is clean; none of the three assertions touches a path written by a conflict resolution, and `git show --cc --name-only 14c9d487fb` shows such a resolution is typically a single runtime path, which a helper that ignores merge commits classifies away

findings.reason: the obligation producer reads followups, so the plan as authored hands out a finished section and never reaches §3, which is what a coordinator dispatching from this plan would act on.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — both §3's Why link (line 43) and the landing comment (line 59) cite `docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-reads-only-its-runs-changes/where-a-review-takes-its-range.html`, which commit 2754cbd2dc deleted (179 deletions, no rename target) and which now exists only as an untracked file in one checkout, so the citation resolves at no committed revision.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's fixture merges an integration branch carrying unrelated files but never a conflict resolution, so the helper's stated "so a conflict resolution the run wrote is kept" is asserted by nothing and an implementation that drops merge-authored paths passes every arm.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3's gate logs go under the run directory and its product change lands in tracked source, not a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `own_changed_paths` and `test_a_review_reads_only_its_runs_changes.py` name the behaviour, match the existing `tests/test_a_review_*` family, and carry no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3's helper enumerates `rev-list --no-merges tip ^integration_ref ^older` and then promises to add "any path a merge commit in that set shows in its combined diff", but a `--no-merges` set contains no merge commit, so the conflict-resolution guarantee cannot execute; reproduced on the plan's own named instance, where the merge `14c9d487fb` is the only commit in `rev-list --merges … ^main` and is absent from the set the helper enumerates.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s3 carries one deliverable (one helper plus the callers that must use it, and the one test that proves it), and its gate is a single verdict on that mechanism.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2 is declared done (line 23, line 38) yet its driving followup f-arroirc-001 is still open and recommends `/reckon-build … §2` (line 47), and no open followup carries §3, so a coordinator driving from followups re-dispatches finished work; s3 also declares no `plan-section-depends-on` for the §2 evidence it consumes (moot now that s2 is done, but it is the relationship the queue orders by).
